mechanism: Evaluates whether the post-state of an action allows a return to the pre-state. Two tests in order: whether the information needed to reconstruct the pre-state still exists, and only then whether restoring it costs less than the caller's declared limit. Returns TRUE for Type 2 decisions (reversible) and FALSE for Type 1 (one-way doors).
gloss: Condition: Can this action be undone?
invariants: A post-state that destroyed the information yields FALSE at any cost limit.
The verdict names the cost limit and information-loss tolerance it was judged against, both {{constraint}}s supplied by the caller.

parameters.name: cost_limit
parameters.description: Maximum acceptable cost to reverse, in a unit the caller states.

failure_modes: False reversibility: the action created externalities the pre-action analysis omitted.
Cost drift: the tolerance was declared before the reversal is attempted.
